payload.entry:
POLICY: ToolRun store keeps 250ms default (zero-means-core-default). Write-open skips SCHEMA_SQL when schema_version, child-observation columns, and required tables (including triage/receipts) are current. One elapsed BusyBudget covers open/WAL/statements/retries; sqlite busy_timeout is sliced to 25ms so sqlite3_open_v2 BUSY is retried. Persist-WAL plus SQLITE_DBCONFIG_NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE so last-close does not exclusive-checkpoint. Retention FS inspect runs after the writer commit. Busy (extended_code) is distinct from corruption; 0-byte in-progress creates are not quarantined. ToolRun PyO3 defaults pass busy_timeout_ms=0; unrelated telemetry bindings stay 250. No wire schema change.

EVIDENCE: unfixed core 89576266 / sase pin 800caef4. WAL BEGIN IMMEDIATE/EXCLUSIVE never busies a reader; show failure is locking_mode=EXCLUSIVE / last-close checkpoint / sqlite3_open_v2 ignoring busy_timeout. just test -p sase_core tool_run::store: 138 pass, 1 ignored. just test -p sase_core_py timeout: 2 pass. sase tool run 368488858077809ada7e7a75e54808a6: our contention and timeout tests green under the full gate; exit 101 is only federation_worker::imp::tests::ipc::listener_creates_private_socket_and_rejects_symlink (known flake sase-1gz). Do not ratchet the sase pin here — caller-integration owns that.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: sase-core check exit 101 is known flake sase-1gz — federation_worker::imp::tests::ipc::listener_creates_private_socket_and_rejects_symlink (unexpected error: federation worker is already running) under the parallel gate; our tool_run store/contention and PyO3 timeout tests passed in the same run 368488858077809ada7e7a75e54808a6.

Rust store contention policy landed in sase-core: skip redundant schema writes on current stores (version + child columns + required tables), bounded BusyBudget retry with 25ms sqlite slices, persist-WAL + NO_CKPT_ON_CLOSE, retention FS after commit, PyO3 ToolRun defaults pass 0. just test -p sase_core tool_run::store 138 pass; just test -p sase_core_py timeout 2 pass; epic-symbols clean. sase tool run 368488858077809ada7e7a75e54808a6 failed only on known flake sase-1gz (gateway listener_creates_private_socket). Default remains 250ms. Pin ratchet left to caller-integration. Did not close parent sase-1ou.2.1 / sase-1ou.2 / sase-18t.

PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP: Wrapper group-kill exit-order flake remains — after/loaded-11 in file:explicit:b13e06f116130351ef4438d2 failed tests/tool/test_wrapper_fidelity.py::test_owner_child_shares_wrapper_group_and_group_kill_leaves_no_survivors at line231 assert not _alive(child_pid), after successful process-group assertions and wrapper.wait following killpg(SIGKILL). No SQLite exception. Rate1/20 loaded,0/10 serial; subsequent complete file passed8/8 and controlled fixed passes3/3 on the same unchanged integrated tree. Likely process exit-order assertion race (waiting for wrapper does not wait for its child), not proven permanent survival. Keep baseline active; outer lander should triage separately from18t. Verification found an in-scope residual core deadline defect: controlled-after.json in file:explicit:b13e06f116130351ef4438d2 has explicit25ms begin waits up to49.951ms. Code confirms enable_wal_mode starts its timer only after initial PRAGMA journal_mode has already spent a SQLite wait. This is a reset, not scheduling tolerance. Local core change moves timer before that probe and adds wal_mode_probe_consumes_conversion_budget (250ms allowance,425ms upper bound with175ms scheduling margin rejects two250ms waits). Preparing red/green core regression, full core check and rebuilt application verification before closure. Core now has a repository commit obligation; host must commit it first and advance primary pin to its actual SHA. No manual commits or invented SHA.
